At last, available in AMAZON. 

👉Links are in the bio.👈

📚📚📚📚📚
I’m excited to announce the release of my book exploring everything that happened behind the scenes of Giant-Size X-Men #1! Written in the informative  style you know from this account, the book is based on testimonies from multiple sources, including the creators themselves, who share insights into the creative process.

📙About the book:
	•	Language: English
	•	Full-color edition: Featuring explanatory images and stunning full-page watercolor portraits of the X-Men by the talented Berto Martínez @berto___martinez .

🛒Where to buy:
The book is already available on Amazon in the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Spain, Italy, Germany, France, the Netherlands, Sweden, and Poland.

🔎Synopsis:

Discover the untold story behind the creation and rise of one of Marvel’s most iconic franchises: the X-Men. This book delves into the pivotal moments that shaped the team, from their early struggles to the transformative relaunch of Giant-Size X-Men #1 in 1975. It explores the creative minds, editorial challenges, and cultural forces that propelled their success, spotlighting key figures like Chris Claremont, Len Wein, and Dave Cockrum.

A highlight of this book is its exclusive, never-before-published interviews with Roy Thomas, Paty Cockrum, and Mike Friedrich, offering unparalleled insights into the franchise’s evolution. Alongside detailed chronologies and in-depth analyses of character development, it focuses on the critical years between 1972 and 1976 that redefined the X-Men.

Also, the book features stunning watercolor portraits by artist Berto Martinez, including unpublished and exclusive X-Men artworks available in print for the first time. This is more than a book—it’s an essential piece of Marvel history for every fan.

In the early 1980s, Uncanny X-Men was one of Marvel’s biggest hits, but the publisher had few spin-offs featuring the team. The New Mutants, created by Chris Claremont and Bob McLeod, was the first. Some readers—and even a few X-Men—called the young team “the X-Babies.” Bill Sienkiewicz helped leave that image behind when he joined Claremont for the “Demon Bear” saga, bringing a striking new visual approach to the series.

“I just wanted to push it even more,” Sienkiewicz recalled. His first drawing of the characters became an ad with the message “Don’t call them X-Babies anymore!” He explained that he began to make them look older while still trying to preserve their youth, and to experiment with “different [and] crazy approaches with the art style.”

Claremont initially persuaded Sienkiewicz to work on a three-issue story, but the collaboration lasted much longer. Their mix of horror and unconventional artwork surprised—and divided—readers, while leading to some of the series’ most innovative stories. The “Demon Bear” saga later inspired the New Mutants film, and Sienkiewicz was invited to visit the set.

Source: Mike Avila, “Don’t Call Them X-Babies! Bill Sienkiewicz on the Art of The New Mutants,” SYFY WIRE, March 25, 2020.

🔸HOW BILL SIENKIEWICZ JOINED THE NEW MUTANTS🔸

Bill Sienkiewicz had already turned down an offer to draw X-Men. He wanted to experiment with techniques that might not suit Marvel’s flagship title. Chris Claremont then pitched him a three-issue story about Dani Moonstar, a demon bear and dream logic. That idea caught Bill’s attention: “Dreams don’t have to make sense, so I could play with illogic or with abstraction or anything.”

Claremont later explained how their collaboration worked: “The paneling and the layout were all his.” He would give Bill the story’s basic shape, then Sienkiewicz would find the images that brought the characters’ inner lives to the page: “who they were inside.”

There was plenty to explore beyond “Demon Bear.” New Mutants #21 turns a girls’ sleepover into the setting for Warlock’s arrival; #25 introduces Legion in a pin-up before his story unfolds in #26–28. The later #29–31 arc brings back Karma under the Shadow King’s influence, trapping Sunspot and Magma in a gladiatorial underworld. And #23–25 takes the team into the strange, sprawling world of Cloak and Dagger. Sienkiewicz’s regular run ended with 31.

Sources: Bill Sienkiewicz interview, PBS (2022)
Chris Claremont Q&A, reproduced by HeroDope (2020)

NewMutants BillSienkiewicz ChrisClaremont XMen MarvelComics

🔸THE NEW MUTANTS: GREAT CHARACTERS, STRANGE ADVENTURES🔸

What went wrong with the New Mutants? The characters were never the problem. Claremont and Louise Simonson created the book to bring the school back into focus. Claremont said they could tell “stories about kids without putting them in the high level of jeopardy that we used in X-Men.”

The team felt distinct from their mentors: Dani carrying her people’s history, Sam from Kentucky, Roberto from Brazil, Rahne reconciling faith with her wolf nature, and Illyana living with what Limbo had done to her. Claremont later described them as “socially, physically in conflict,” because none belonged where they were. He wanted readers to watch them grow and change.

But the adventures often pulled elsewhere. Some stranger detours:

1. Lila Cheney, interstellar rock star, plans to steal Earth and sell it to aliens.
2. Rahne and Roberto become dark and light monsters after receiving the drugs that created Cloak and Dagger.
3. The team is swept into an alien gladiator arena inside a Dyson sphere, with a horse-headed villain.
4. Mojo turns the young mutants into adult TV stars with powers.

These plots could push the school and friendship stories aside. That explains part of the disappointment: you cared about the characters’ personal struggles, then the plot took them into an adventure that seemed to belong in another comic.

Bill Sienkiewicz’s art heightened that strangeness. In the Demon Bear saga, story and image become dreamlike, unsettling and symbolic. For some readers, that made the series unique; for others, the action harder to follow.

Claremont’s regular run ended with #54. He later said his planned six-month break was “originally only going to be for six months until we got Excalibur out of the way.”

Art by Salvador Larroca for Spain Comics Forum edition. 

Sources: Claremont, Comics Creators on X-Men (Titan, 2006); Comic Culture, PBS (2026); Comics Interview #56 (1988).

#NewMutants #ChrisClaremont #MarvelComics XMen

🔹DID A LATE DAREDEVIL #1 REALLY CREATE THE AVENGERS?🔹

The familiar story goes like this: Marvel planned to launch X-Men and Daredevil in 1963, filling two new publishing slots granted by its distributor. When Bill Everett fell badly behind on Daredevil #1, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby hurriedly assembled Marvel’s existing heroes and created The Avengers to prevent the reserved press slot from going unused.

Comics historian Mark Evanier supports that account: Everett could not meet the deadline, so Marvel postponed Daredevil and produced Avengers #1 as its replacement. Avengers and X-Men consequently reached newsstands together in July 1963, while Daredevil did not appear until early 1964. 

But Tom Brevoort later uncovered evidence complicating the legend. A reprint preserves the production code X-337 on Avengers #1, while X-Men #1 carries X-401. Because Marvel generally assigned these numbers sequentially, this suggests Avengers was already in production considerably earlier—not improvised after Daredevil collapsed. Brevoort therefore considers it possible that X-Men, not Avengers, ultimately occupied Daredevil’s intended slot. 

The safest conclusion: Everett’s lateness definitely disrupted Marvel’s 1963 plans, but the popular claim that The Avengers exists solely because Daredevil missed its deadline remains an attractive—and unproven—origin story.

🎨 slide 1 Brett Booth tribute , slide 2 Alex Ross tribute 
Sources: Tom Brevoort on the production-code evidence⁠￼ · Mark Evanier on the traditional account⁠￼ · Marvel: ⁠￼The Avengers⁠￼ 1⁠￼

🔸BETSY WAS ALREADY “BUTTERFLY”🔸

Marvel has announced that Betsy Braddock will be called Butterfly in Maximum X-Men. Tom Brevoort confirmed the change in his newsletter, listing “Betsy Braddock (formerly Psylocke and Captain Britain, and here called Butterfly)” on the team’s roster. For Spanish readers, the name feels familiar: in Spain, she was already Mariposa Mental (“Mental Butterfly”) in the comics that introduced her to the X-Men in the late 1980s.

There’s a lovely linguistic echo here, too. Psylocke comes from (or sounds like) Psyche Lock. Ancient Greek ψυχή (psychē) means “soul” or “life”; the Liddell–Scott–Jones lexicon also records the rarer meaning “butterfly or moth.” It’s a fitting connection for a telepath whose powers have so often been represented by a psychic butterfly. In English, Betsy gets a new codename for this series. In Spanish, we’ve known her as Mariposa🦋 for decades.

Sources: Tom Brevoort, “Monofocus 2”⁠￼ · LSJ, ψυχή⁠￼ · The Uncanny X-Men⁠￼ #213, Spanish-edition details⁠￼

#XMen #BetsyBraddock #Psylocke #MaximumXMen MarvelComics

🔹X-MEN NEWS FROM NYCC 2026🔹

Marvel brought news for the comics, the Midnight line and X-Men ’97:

• Magneto gets a new series. Magneto: End of Days is an eight-issue prestige miniseries by Brian Michael Bendis and Andrea Sorrentino, launching in February 2027. It will revisit key moments from Magneto’s past and look at how his choices might shape his future.

• X-Orcists is going ongoing. The supernatural team’s book will continue beyond its initial run. In issue #3, due in January 2027, Elsa Bloodstone joins Magik, Madelyne Pryor, Juggernaut and Bloodline as they hunt a demon from Limbo.

• More from Midnight X-Men. NYCC revealed new designs by R. B. Silva, including a bat-like Beast and a crystalline Iceman. The January 2027 issue, written by Jonathan Hickman with art by Matteo Buffagni, teases a conspiracy and threats from both humans and mutants.

• Maystorm is coming back. Peach Momoko announced a new book featuring the character, but said it won’t take place in the Ultimate Universe where she first appeared. No title or release date was given.

• A new way to collect Claremont’s run. Marvel Brick, a paperback compendium line planned for the second half of 2027, will launch with Uncanny X-Men: All New, All Different, beginning with the era that followed Giant-Size X-Men #1.

• Rogue and Gambit’s wedding is coming to X-Men ’97. The season 3 footage shown at NYCC also teased mutant registration checkpoints, the return of the Brotherhood, and appearances by She-Hulk and Deadpool. The season is expected in 2027.

Sources: AIPT, Bleeding Cool, ICv2.

#XMen #MarvelComics #XMen97 ClassicXMen NYCC2026

🔸ALPHA FLIGHT WAS CREATED TO FIGHT THE X-MEN🔸

Alpha Flight was never conceived as the beginning of a Canadian spin-off. John Byrne later described its original purpose very simply: “Alpha Flight existed only as a team assembled to fight the X-Men.”

The idea began with Wolverine. Dave Cockrum had suggested that the Canadian government would hardly accept losing its expensive investment to Xavier’s team, so Ottawa would logically send someone to bring him back. Byrne already had Guardian, Snowbird and Shaman in various forms from his fan days; he redesigned them and added Northstar and Aurora, whose super-speed countered Nightcrawler’s teleportation, and Sasquatch, who could match Colossus physically.

Although Byrne created civilian identities and fragments of backstory, he still regarded them primarily as opponents capable of surviving a prolonged battle with the X-Men. After their full appearance in X-Men #120–121, however, the characters became popular enough for Marvel to request a series. Byrne resisted because he felt they lacked depth: “I just didn’t see much that could be done with them.” He finally agreed when he realised Marvel would probably give the book to someone else.

Alpha Flight #1 arrived in 1983, forcing Byrne to transform characters designed for one confrontation into the protagonists of their own world. One of Marvel’s most durable mutant-related teams therefore grew from a practical storytelling problem: how do you build opponents who can credibly take on the X-Men?

Sources: John Byrne, “What’s the story behind Alpha Flight’s creation?”, Byrne Robotics FAQ, July 16, 2008; Marvel, Alpha Flight by John Byrne Omnibus.

#AlphaFlight #JohnByrne #ClassicXMen Wolverine XMenHistory

🔸DAVE COCKRUM’S “BIGGEST MISTAKE”🔸

When Dave Cockrum returned to Uncanny X-Men after John Byrne’s departure, he was enthusiastic about drawing the team again. His second run began with #145, but Cockrum also had an original project, The Futurians, sitting on Jim Shooter’s desk. When Marvel finally approved it, Chris Claremont and editor Louise Simonson encouraged him to pursue the project he seemed more excited about.

Cockrum left X-Men without yet knowing how valuable Marvel’s new royalty system could be. Payments arrived nine months after an issue went on sale, so he had received nothing when he made his decision. “That was probably the biggest mistake of my life,” he later admitted. His first royalty cheque arrived only after his departure: “When the first one came it was $2,000 right out of the air!”

The Futurians never achieved comparable success, while X-Men continued growing into Marvel’s dominant franchise. Cockrum said that if he had known even $2,000 a month was coming, “you couldn’t have pried me off that book with a crowbar.” His departure was a creative gamble, but also a decision made before delayed royalty statements revealed what staying on X-Men was really worth.

Source: Dave Cockrum interview by Jon B. Cooke, Comic Book Artist #6, TwoMorrows, 1998.

#DaveCockrum #UncannyXMen #ClassicXMen TheFuturians XMenHistory

🔹 THE X-MEN ARRIVE IN FINLAND 🔹

When Ryhmä-X #1 hit Finnish newsstands in late 1984, it marked the first time the X-Men received their own local comic. Published by Semic, the debut issue used the cover of X-Men #126 (Dave Cockrum & Terry Austin) and reprinted Claremont and Byrne’s Savage Land storyline—material that Finnish readers had already seen in Ihmeneloset, but now heavily edited to fit a 68-page format.

Despite the backtracking in continuity and the “editing chainsaw” approach, Ryhmä-X quickly became a cult publication. Copies of the first issue are notoriously rare today, especially in good condition, making it one of the most sought-after early Marvel releases in Finland.

🎨: #XMen #RyhmäX #MarvelFinland #ClassicXMen #Claremont #JohnByrne #DaveCockrum #ComicHistory

Seeing this 1987 Critic’s Choice File guide, devoted to Uncanny X-Men #111–128, immediately takes me back to what many of us consider the X-Men’s golden age: the Claremont and Byrne years.

Terry Austin’s inks gave Byrne’s pencils that clean, precise finish that became instantly recognisable, while the bold primary colours made every page demand your attention. For me, this artwork brings back the wonderful feeling of discovering these characters almost at the same pace as their creators were developing them, gradually revealing their personalities and building extraordinary histories around them.

Storm was a claustrophobic goddess, a former thief who refused to kill; Cyclops, a restrained and tormented leader driven by an almost impossible level of self-discipline; Banshee, the experienced former Interpol agent and man of the world; Nightcrawler, the playful and deeply human soul of the team; and Colossus, the shy Russian farm boy still overwhelmed by his own strength.

And Wolverine… well, Wolverine was already very much Wolverine, although his past, age and even his place within the team remained uncertain. That sense that any of them could still grow, change or reveal something unexpected was part of the magic. They had not yet become completely defined icons: we were watching them become the X-Men.

#XMen #UncannyXMen #ChrisClaremont #JohnByrne TerryAustin

🔸ANN NOCENTI’S WEIRD X-MEN🔸

When Marvel began reprinting the early Claremont era in Classic X-Men, the new backup stories opened a space that Ann Nocenti believed should be used for something very different from the main series. She and Claremont took turns writing them, but Nocenti remembers their guiding question as: “What is the weird X-Men story that you’d never be able to tell in the main book?”

That approach explains why her stories often feel so unusual. Instead of reproducing the large-scale action of Uncanny X-Men, Nocenti could isolate a character, explore an uncomfortable idea or follow a surreal premise without having to serve the momentum of the monthly series. John Bolton’s freedom as an artist supported that atmosphere, but the creative impulse Nocenti describes was already clear: these backups were allowed to be strange.

She also connects them to her wider contribution as X-Men editor. Having learned from Louise Simonson, Nocenti saw her role as helping to channel Claremont’s enormous supply of ideas and decide which ones should become stories. In Classic X-Men, that same instinct produced a small experimental corner inside what appeared, at first glance, to be a reprint comic.

Source: Chris Hassan, “X-Men Monday #202 — Ann Nocenti Talks ‘Storm’,” AIPT, May 8, 2023.

#ClassicXMen #AnnNocenti #ChrisClaremont #XMenHistory MarvelComics

Pakistan’s favorite sweet, made foolproof! This 14 August, make soft, juicy Gulab Jamun with simple ingredients and Asad Memon’s tried-and-tested tips for perfect results every time!
Made with #Dalda, our trusted recipe partner. Celebrate Pakistan with a little sweetness! #FoodFusion #HappyCookingToYou #GulabJamun #14August 

Ingredients:
Prepare Sugar Syrup:
-Sugar 2 Cups (450g)
-Water 2 & ½ Cups
-Hari elaichi (Green cardamom) 6 
-Lemon juice 1 tsp
Prepare Gulab Jamun:
-Anda (Egg) 1
-Doodh (Milk) 3 tbs
-Dalda VTF Banaspati melted 2 tbs
-Milk powder 2 Cups (200g)
-Maida (All-purpose flour) 3 tbs
-Sooji (Semolina) 2 tsp
-Baking powder 1 tsp 
-Dalda VTF Banaspati for frying 
-Pista (Pistachios) chopped as required

Direction:
Prepare Sugar Syrup:
-In a wok, add sugar, water, green cardamom, lemon juice, & turn on the flame.
-Mix well & cook on medium flame until sugar dissolves completely.
Prepare Gulab Jamun:
-In a bowl, add egg, milk, banaspati, & whisk well.
-In another bowl, add milk powder, all-purpose flour, fine semolina, baking powder, and mix well
-Add prepared egg mixture, mix until dough is formed.
-Cover & let it rest for 10 minutes.
-Take 1 tbs (18g) of dough & make crack free balls, (Makes: 24).
-In a wok, add banaspati & bring it to heat. (120-130C)
-Fry on low flame until golden; keep mixing to get an even color.
-Take them out, add to hot sugar syrup, cover & rest for 1-2 hours.
-Garnish with chopped pistachios & serve warm!

Butter Noodles with amazingly spiced Chicken, a combination worth trying. #happycookingtoyou #foodfusion #digitalammi #arraywah

Ingredients:
Prepare Chicken:
-Chicken fillets 2 (approx. 350g)

-Himalayan pink salt ½ tsp or to taste
-Lemon juice 1 tbs

-Lehsan (Garlic) chopped 1 tbs
-Maida (All-purpose flour) ½ tbs
-Chicken yakhni (Stock) ¼ Cup
-Hara dhania (Fresh coriander) chopped 1 tsp 
Prepare Butter Noodles:
-Cooking oil 1 tsp
-Makhan (Butter) 60g
-Lehsan (Garlic) chopped 2 tbs
-Chicken yakhni (Stock) ½ Cup
-Kali mirch powder (Black pepper powder) ½ tsp
-Lal mirch (Red chilli) crushed 1 tsp
-Dried parsley 1 tsp
-Himalayan pink salt ½ tsp or to taste 
-Dried oregano ½ tsp
-Spaghetti 200g (boiled as per pack’s instructions)
-Hara dhania (Fresh coriander) chopped handful
-Lehsan (Garlic) fried 
-Hara dhania (Fresh coriander) chopped

Directions:
Prepare Chicken:
-Pound chicken fillet from one side with the help of meat mallet.
-In a bowl,add red chilli crushed,black pepper powder,pink salt,lemon juice & mix well.
-Add chicken fillet,coat well,cover & marinate for 15-20 minutes. 
-In a frying pan,add cooking oil,butter & let it melt.
-Add garlic & sauté for a minute.
-Add marinated fillets & sprinkle all-purpose flour on both sides.
-Add chicken stock,cover & cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes then cook on medium flame from both sides until it dries up. 
-Sprinkle fresh coriander then cut into slices & set aside.
Prepare Butter Noodles:
-In a frying pan,add cooking oil,butter & let it melt.
-Add garlic & sauté for a minute.
-Add chicken stock,black pepper powder,red chilli crushed,dried parsley,pink salt,dried oregano,mix well & cook for a minute.
-Add boiled spaghetti,fresh coriander & toss well.
-Sprinkle fried garlic,fresh coriander & serve!

A cool, coconut-infused masterpiece—soft, soaked, and layered with tropical sweetness in every chilled bite! This Brazilian Coconut Cold Cake is pure, silky indulgence that melts effortlessly in your mouth! #happycookingtoyou #foodfusion #araywahh 

Ingredients:
Prepare Coconut Cake:
-Anday (Eggs) 4 (room temperature)
-Sugar 1 Cup
-Cooking oil 1/3 Cup
-Vanilla essence ½ tbs
-Maida (All-purpose flour) 1 & ½ Cup
-Baking powder 1 tsp
-Himalayan pink salt ¼ tsp
-Khopra (Desiccated coconut) ½ Cup
-Doodh (Milk) ½ Cup (room temperature)
Prepare Coconut Milk Syrup:
-Doodh (Milk) 1 & ½ Cup
-Condensed milk 150ml
-Coconut milk powder 50g
-Khopra (Desiccated coconut)

Directions:
Prepare Coconut Cake:
-In a bowl,add eggs,sugar & beat until well combined. 
-Add cooking oil,vanilla essence & beat well.
-Place a sieve on the bowl,add all-purpose flour,baking powder,pink salt & sift well.
-Add desiccated coconut & mix well.
-Add milk & mix well.
-On greased 9x9” baking dish lined with baking paper,pour prepared batter & tap few times. 
-Bake in preheated oven at 170°C for 40-45 minutes or until skewer comes out clean.
-Let it cool.
-Trim edges & cut into square pieces.
Prepare Coconut Milk Syrup:
-In a jug,add milk,condensed milk,coconut milk powder & whisk well.
-Now dip cake pieces in prepared coconut milk syrup & coat well from all sides with desiccated coconut.
-Wrap the cake pieces in aluminium foil & refrigerate until chilled.
-Pour coconut milk syrup & serve!

-Add mozzarella cheese on the sides of egg & poke the egg yolk with the help of wooden skewer.
-Bake in preheated oven at 190C for 10-12 minutes (on both grills).
-Sprinkle fresh coriander & serve with tea.

Recipe in English

Homemade Crispy Mong Daal
Ingredients:
-Mong daal (Yellow lentil) 1 & ½ Cup
-Water as required
-Cooking oil 1 tsp
-Iodized Himalayan pink salt ½ tsp
-Iodized Himalayan pink salt to taste

Direction:
-Wash moong daal properly & soak for 3-4 hours.
-Now drain the water; in boiling water, add soaked moong daal & boil on medium flame for 5-6 minutes or until tender but not mushy.
-Now Strain properly & spread on a kitchen towel, then pat dry.
-In a bowl, add dried mong daal, cooking oil, and pink salt; mix well
-Place the liner in the air-fryer bucket & add moong daal & air-fry at 160°C for 18-20 minutes.
-Transfer it to a bowl, immediately add pink salt, mix well; moong daal nimco is ready!

Homemade Crispy Chana Daal
Ingredients:

Magnifique premier long métrage d’animation de Louis Clichy, Le Corset avait remporté le Prix spécial du Jury à #Cannes2026, avant d’être trois fois primé au Festival d’Annecy. Depuis, l’histoire, inspirée de celle du réalisateur, de ce « jeune garçon qui penche » n’a cessé de convaincre la presse et le public des festivals. Tourné en prises de vues réelles dans la Beauce et dessiné à l’aquarelle et à l’encre de Chine, le film séduit par son esthétique orginale autant que par son récit universel d’émancipation et de résilience. Une révélation à ne pas manquer en salle dès aujourd’hui !
-----
Louis Clichy’s magnificent debut animated feature, Le Corset, won the Jury Special Prize at #Cannes2026 before going on to receive three awards at the Annecy Festival. Since then, the story of a “young boy who leans”, inspired by the director’s own experience, has continued to win over festival critics and audiences alike. Filmed on location in the Beauce region of France and brought to life through watercolour and Chinese ink, the film captivates with its distinctive visual style and its universal story of emancipation and resilience. A revelation not to be missed in cinemas from today!

Avec Minotaure, récompensé du Grand Prix de #Cannes2026 et choisi pour représenter la France aux #Oscars2027, Andreï Zviaguintsev transpose La Femme infidèle de Claude Chabrol dans la Russie de 2022, au moment où éclate la guerre contre l'Ukraine. Gleb, chef d’entreprise prospère, vit avec sa femme et leur fils dans une ville de province. L’effondrement de leur existence soigneusement construite va rapidement basculer dans la violence.
Un drame familial et politique virtuose, à découvrir en salle en France dès aujourd’hui.
-----
With Minotaur, winner of the Grand Prix at #Cannes2026 and selected to represent France at the #Oscars2027, Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s The Unfaithful Wife to Russia in 2022, as the war in Ukraine breaks out.
Gleb, a successful businessman, lives with his wife and son in a provincial town. The collapse of a carefully constructed life quickly spirals into violence. A virtuoso family and political drama, Minotaur opens in French cinemas today.

latestPosts.caption: 馬斯克新款特斯拉會飛，讓全中國網友崩潰，惡意起飛，讓我們華為顏面盡失，中國百萬豪車連煞車踏板都會被踩斷，美國人已經能讓車飛起來了。
中國人崩潰，請道士作法，讓颱風轉向台灣，結果直撲大陸，村子被滅頂。

🇹🇼 中華民國115年，雙十國慶快樂！

這兩張照片，是我在中共領事館前，舉起青天旗的畫面，那一刻我有很深的感觸，甚至我親自走進中共總大使館自首，而分裂的，讓國民黨淪落至此的，請韓國瑜院長記得，是繼承中華蘇維埃共和國血脈的中共國。

我們可以對歷史有不同的理解，對國家的名字有不同的情感，甚至對未來有不同的想像。但至少有一件事情，我希望所有台灣人都能站在一起：我們的命運，不能由北京決定。

民主最珍貴的地方，就是允許我們不一樣。今天我們能夠自由爭論未來，是因為前人替我們守住了現在。如果連眼前的自由都失去了，再美好的理想，也只會成為遙不可及的夢。

守護今天，不代表停止想像未來。因為真正值得捍衛的，從來都是這片土地上的人民，有權選擇自己的未來，祝福台灣，也祝福所有仍在追求自由的人們。

願有一天，自由不再需要用勇氣來證明，不論你想稱作台灣，還是中華民國，總之不可能是🇨🇳中共國，這是底線。我是台灣人！￼

大家注意力都在選舉，但拜託大家注意一下。就是疑似「肺鼠疫」在俄羅斯西伯利亞，出現了。西伯利亞下方就是中國，台灣人去年到訪中國旅遊人次高達三百多萬。

最弔詭的是中俄，在八月底於「東北黑龍江」演習這場鼠疫了，而參與致詞方，其之一人正是該爆發病毒實驗室的所長。

川普的回應：這所謂病毒比以前更強，我們以前對付的治療效果沒有用了。當然我注意到我們政府也非常快速的開記者，研議會做出應對方針。￼

洋流人潮不輸凱道
人多到我走不出去，喝光三瓶水
台北市民把沈伯洋puma 送進市政府
讓我們的首都，越來越國際化。￼

我總共花了一小時才走出去…

以前看吳奇隆拍軍教片，熱血沸騰
捍衛台灣、保衛中華民國🇹🇼
結果現在跑去天安門舉🇨🇳五星旗
你倒是入籍拿身分證啊

歲月是一把殺豬刀，無論內心還是外表。
圖片附上的是吳奇隆參演的軍教片

富邦今天表示，因為吳奇隆身體不舒服
所以取消了10/4在新莊的開球典禮。

去年，很多人只看了後半段十秒鐘，就說我八炯「太極端」、「主動找民眾麻煩」。

一年後，我又看見了這張臉。今天他因為留言「希望沈伯洋的女兒遇到小燈泡」被找出金融夜身分，任職公司也出面回應，當事人已經自請離職。

而我看到他的第一眼，就認出來了。

去年罷免連署期間，就是這個人出現在我們的連署現場，與志工發生衝突。

當天現場有老人、有小孩，也有孕婦，我上前制止、把人請離現場。

結果後來網路上大量流傳的，卻只剩下我最激動、最大聲的那十秒。

前面發生什麼事，沒人看了。

所以今天我不想叫任何人「相信八炯」。

我只希望大家把完整畫面看一次。

政治立場可以不同，可以討厭我，可以罵我，但不要因為一段被切掉前因後果的影片，就替一個人定罪。

如果那天在現場的是你的爸爸媽媽、你的老婆，甚至是你的孩子——

有人站出來制止衝突，最後卻被剪成「主動欺負民眾的人」。

你會希望大家只看那十秒，還是把事情從頭看到尾？

一年後，我還是會做一樣的選擇。

回花蓮遇到副總統的機率是多少😂

很多人可能只認得蕭副總統
但站在旁邊的林則葹、陳思伃
都曾經是蕭美琴的國會助理

現在再站到一起，三個人的身分都變了
蕭美琴先後成為駐美代表、副總統
林則葹後來當選花蓮縣議員，拚連任
陳思伃這次也走到了第一線參選議員
兩人卻不擔心相互搶票，在同一個選區合作

對我來說，最好看的不是誰站在哪個位置
而是十幾年的時間，大家還能站在一起

11/28，花蓮人回家投票吧￼

館長去不了美國，看習近平和彭麗媛夫人
中國人代替館長去華盛頓，用大聲公播放這段館長的影片
給習近平夫妻聽看看，祝福館長在中國生意新隆！
台灣桃園人，持續帶台灣人去辦理中共國身分證！並且成立台商園區，帶不少台灣年輕人過去當抖音網紅，詐騙、貸款、洗錢。請內政部依法開除台灣護照，註銷這些壞人的中華民國國籍。

一週內，第三個了，又一名在台灣負責接應、協助台灣人申辦中國身分證的「接頭人」被挖出來了。這背後到底藏著多少人、串起多大的九合一危機？

到現在，依然沒有「任何一家新聞媒體」跟進報導。麻煩大家把影片裡的證據截圖、轉發出去，不用提到我八炯，我不需要流量，我只要這件事壓不下去。￼

latestPosts.caption: Grateful for these lovely reviews, but more important to me is that #climbers are finding my books to be practical and digestible. 🙏🙏
Super grateful for all the feedback on my books. Keep it coming and let me know what you found most useful in the comments 👇
Guess where you can find all 3 of my books? Yep, the lovely @indyclimbingwall shop. Have a flick through whilst you are resting between problems!

So, despite a horse-related finger injury in the last week of the aggregate, I managed to come joint 3rd in my category with my bouldering buddy, Suzie.  We had such a blast climbing together, spending days and nights figuring out beta to work around our respective weaknesses and egging each other on.  Suzie is inspiring to climb with - she has determination and grit in spades and is mega strong.  Having supportive friends to bring out the best in you is so important - having fun and social support are good predictors of motivation, and we had plenty this winter!  Huge thanks to the Indy team for always being welcoming, setting some great problems and lending us brushes and beta when we needed it 😍

Instructors and Coaches with mental health difficulties and/or neurodiversity - I need your help!
I'm delivering a talk at the MT conference next week on reasonable adjustments to training courses and assessments.  I know a lot of you will either not have been aware that you could ask for reasonable adjustments, or felt like you couldn't ask, or perhaps you have asked and been told 'no'. I'd love to hear about your experiences of what was difficult for you on training or assessment linked to mental health or neurodiversity, what might have helped, and whether you did or did not have reasonable adjustments. 
You can get in touch in confidence by DM'ing me, or emailing me directly. I won't share anything without your explicit consent, but it will help to make sure I am targeting my talk at the issues people face. Many thanks

Pretty chuffed to be joint 3rd with Suzie - she is a proper powerhouse and the only way I keep up with her is by being a few inches taller 😆 But more important than the result for me is the improvement I have felt this winter, and I actually feel like I'm bouldering better than I ever have done - experience helps with technique, friends help with confidence to try things you think are too hard, and the extra gym sessions I think have paid off.  Proof that age is just a number if you are psyched, and working out the most pleasing sequence is always the thing I love the most (just wish my brain didn't do this when I was trying to get to sleep!)
Massive thanks to all the @indyclimbingwall team - the problems were fab and a really great range of styles, the staff are always super friendly and welcoming and they even put up a sign to discourage beta spraying 😍 plus the coffee is A1.

Confidence is also a product of your social support

"Houston, we have a problem!" 
The first people I texted when my naughty pony slammed a heavy wooden gate into my finger were my two climbing buddies.  I am a bit gutted to be off climbing for a while, but I have been thinking about how important it is to climb with people who are there for you through thick and thin, wobbles and all.  Rauni and Suzie are just the perfect climbing partners - we all climb around the same level but with different strengths, I can be vulnerable in front of them and they give me such confidence to experiment, make mistakes and laugh at myself.  Performance wise, it's been great to see that at 51 I can still improve and have broken my boulder grade plateau this year, mostly I think due to their support, commitment and consistency.  Despite our limited time, we make dates to climb and stick to it (injury and illness aside!) and we can show up in whatever state of mind or fatigue, knowing that we can find some fun stuff to work on together, turning lemons into lemonade with surprising regularity. 
If you can't be yourself, tears, wobbles and all, with your climbing partner, then think about the cost to your confidence of not feeling accepted, just as you are.  We can only step out of our comfort zone when we feel safe to do so, so if your belaytionships are not giving you psychological safety, maybe its time to find some new climbing pals.

Highlights for me were Meg’s fantastic talk on healing through #climbing and the smiles on everyone’s faces as they unlocked new moves 💪 and my Confident Climbing Workbook made its first foray into the wild! DM me if you’d like a copy as it’s a small print run and not in my shop yet!

Are you making the most of any positive climbing experiences you have? Not just the sends or the onsights, but the small glimmers of progress, the stylish move, the perfect gear placement, the feeling of flow? Often we spend too much time criticising ourselves and not enough time noticing the small things we do well.  Making this noticing a focus can really help build your confidence over time.

Confidence is not a personality trait, but something you build over time.  The biggest mistake I see people making is to try imagine they can force confidence by pushing out of their comfort zone before they are actually ready or feel psychologically safe to do so.  In reality, most of our confidence comes from our past experiences, so think for a minute, have your climbing experiences been mostly confidence building or mostly fear reinforcing? With anxious experiences 'weighing' more than confidence-inspiring ones, we need to be careful that we balance plenty of skill building and in-comfort zone experiences with fewer stretch zone experiences. 
I'll be covering this and more @womensclimbing  WCS26, and bringing along a few tester versions of my new confident climbing workbook.  See you there!

Fall practice should be the cherry on top of the cake, not the cake itself! If there is a big gap between your potential (you at your best) and what you can do on lead due to anxiety, then you will benefit more from learning anxiety management techniques first.  I'll be covering this at WCS26 in my workshops.

Not long to go before my fave event of the year, WCS26 ! I'll be delivering a practical workshop on taming fear and building confidence, and bringing along a pilot copy of my new workbook, Confident Climbing for people to try out and give feedback on.  Let me know if you are going to be there!

latestPosts.caption:
#Installation Un caballo sin jinete reposa en el cielo de Madrid 🐎⁠
⁠
Con "El rumor de la discordia", @gonzalolebrija transforma el simbolismo de las escultura ecuestres que habitan el centro de las ciudades desafiando así las narrativas tradicionales de victoria y poder. En cambio, instala un purasangre desprovisto de riendas, silla y pedestal convencional, en un instante imposible entre la caída y el reposo.⁠
⁠
📍 Plaza del Carmen, Madrid.⁠
➡️ Cesión temporal del @thompsonmadridhotel al Ayuntamiento de Madrid.⁠
📸 Oak Taylor-Smith

#Installation 🏛️✨ Transparencia y memoria histórica en el centro de Roma. Con SELVA, @edoardotresoldiofficial interviene la Piazza Mignanelli a través de una pieza encargada por la @fondazionevggg. Dieciséis columnas transparentes que se integran en el espacio dejando ver lo que hay en él: la luz, la arquitectura romana y el propio pulso de la ciudad.⁠
⁠
📍 Piazza Mignanelli, Roma.⁠
📅 Hasta enero de 2027.

#Exhibition ¿Cómo suena la lluvia al transformarse en música?⁠
⁠
Por primera vez al aire libre, la icónica instalación Clinamen de @celesteboursiermougenot llega a Atenas de la mano de @onassis.foundation. La obra, que ya en si misma despliega un paisaje acuático y sonoro a través del choque de los boles, se adapta ahora al pulso de la ciudad y al cielo de Ática: si llueve, el agua se suma a la propia partitura. ⁠
⁠
📍 @onassis.stegi.⁠
📅 Hasta 5 de diciembre de 2026⁠
📹️ @celesteboursiermougenot

#Installation Con Mère We Sea, Prouvost Laure (@studioprouvostsocialclub) convierte la capilla de De Noker en un entorno fluido suspendido entre la memoria y la imaginación. La instalación combina piezas de vidrio suspendidas, proyecciones y un paisaje sonoro de voces que fusionan gestos de cuidado y la  propia vida marina, invitando al espectador a habitar un espacio inmersivo comisariado por Sofia Lemos para la @contourbiennale.⁠
⁠
📍 De Noker, Malinas (Bélgica)⁠
📅  Hasta el 1 de noviembre de 2026⁠
📷️ Filip Claessens

#Installation ¿Es posible romper las fronteras mentales a través de una cadena humana gigante? 🤝🌍⁠
⁠
Tras su paso por otras grandes ciudades como París o El Cairo, @saype_artiste inaugura un nuevo capitulo de su proyecto Beyond Walls en San Francisco. Una intervención monumental realizada con pintura biodegradable sobre césped que dibuja manos entrelazadas como símbolo de unión, pluralidad y derechos civiles. ⁠
⁠
📍 Yerba Buena Gardens (@visityerbabuenasf)⁠
📷️ @fssanfrancisco, @saype_artiste & @bubbagraph415

#LaMasíaGallery @esthermiquel nos habla de su práctica artística, de cómo fusiona silencio y ruido y de lo que persigue con su nueva exposición "Interlude"⁠.⁠
⁠
Recuerda que puedes visitar la exposición en La Masía Gallery, en la segunda planta de la flagship store de @nudeproject en Barcelona. ¡No te la pierdas!⁠
⁠
📍 Carrer dels Boters, 6, Barcelona, planta 2.⁠
📅 Hasta el 1 de noviembre de 2026.

#Exhibition Últimos días para visitar "Dulce venganza", la primera muestra individual de Felix Gonzalez-Torres en Madrid.⁠
⁠
La obra de González-Torres convierte experiencias profundamente personales, como el amor o la pérdida, en materia creativa desde la cual interpelar al visitante. Es este el que completa la obra, motivo por el cual no exiten dos formas iguales de acercarse a la misma. ⁠
⁠
📍@museoreinasofia⁠
📆 Abierta al público hasta el 12 de octubre de 2026

#Installation En PATIO, el colectivo @peniqueproductions toma el Palacio de los Torrero (sede del @coaaragon en Zaragoza) mediante una membrana plástica de color rojo que infla el espacio y crea un diálogo con el patrimonio. Invitados por @jpenaibanez de @concentricofestival, la intervención celebra la apertura de @fundara_arquitectura transformando la percepción de un lugar emblemático.⁠
⁠
📸 @peniqueproductions⁠
📅 Hasta el 18 de octubre⁠ de 2026⁠
#Scanningtheartist con @rom.mo. Hablamos sobre chistes malos, gatitos y la nostalgia como la mejor herramienta para crear 🐈️⁠

#Installation Seis obras clave de @francois.morellet dialogan con el espacio del @chateauversailles. Destaca entre ellas "Lamentable", una de sus instalaciones de neón más icónicas, donde la forma perfecta de un círculo se fragmenta y cae derrotada al suelo. Una pieza irónica y aparentemente desordenada que desafía la solemnidad del palacio con una mezcla única de absurdo, elegancia y poesía.⁠
⁠
📍 Hasta el 1 de noviembre. de 2026.⁠
📸 @tomagarnier & @chateauversailles

#Installation ¿Qué ocurre cuando un edificio famoso por su transparencia tiene que cubrirse? ⁠
⁠
Recordando el trabajo de @canepapa con motivo de la restauración del Palacio de Cristal, que transformó la estructura de andamios en un lienzo monumental. Así nace Fardo, una intervención inspirada en los textiles prehispánicos de su Perú natal que, por un tiempo, reemplazará el cristal del emblemático monumento por una piel llena de patrones y simbolismo. Una propuesta que nos invita a detenernos frente a un hito en pausa y descubrir la belleza de lo que se resguarda de la mirada pública.⁠

Reverse Sear 🤝 Meat Sweats

Steps:
1. Pat steak dry and season generously w/ salt
2. Bake on a cooling rack at 275°F until internal temp hits 105–110°F
3. Get a skillet (or grill) ripping hot
4. Pat steak dry and sear 45–60 sec per side
5. Optional: butter, garlic & rosemary baste
6. Pull at 120–125°F
7. Rest 5 minutes, slice & enjoy
___________

Ingredients:
- 1.5 - 2 lbs of chicken (breasts or thighs)
- 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar
- 1/3 cup olive oil
- 3 tbsp maple syrup
- 2 tsp Dijon mustard
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp fresh thyme 
- 1/8 tsp cayenne pepper
- 1/4 tsp salt & pepper each

Pork butt burnt ends 🐷🔥

Ingredients:
- 5 lbs boneless pork butt 
- 1 cup BBQ sauce 
- 1/2 cup BBQ seasoning 
- 1/4 cup brown sugar 
- 4 tbsp honey
- 1/4 cup yellow mustard 
- 2 sticks of butter 

Steps:
1. Cube pork and toss with mustard + ½ the seasoning
2. Smoke at 225°F for ~3 hours, until ~175°F internal and desired color
3. Add pork to a tray and top with butter, brown sugar, remaining seasoning, honey, and BBQ sauce and cover
4. Smoke at 300°F for ~1 hour, until ~200°F internal
5. Let cool slightly and enjoy!

Si cada semana persigues datos en Excel, rehaces informes y llegas tarde…
el problema no es tu esfuerzo.

En el Bootcamp Analytics & Business Intelligence de Smartclimbs no aprendes solo Power BI.

Aprendes a:
• Diseñar KPIs con criterio

• Construir dashboards que sí se usan

Todo con IA como copiloto y aplicado a casos reales.

6 semanas. 70 horas. Proyecto aplicado.

Solicita el programa y evalúa si es el siguiente paso para ti.

Cuando analizas “ventas del mes”… ¿hablas de orden, factura, despacho o cobro?
Si tu modelo usa una sola fecha, estás mezclando todo.
Aquí te enseño a separarlo en Power BI. ✅
#PowerBI #DAX #BI

📊 Si tu lista de métricas en Power BI se parece a la lista del súper… necesitas carpetas. 🧠🗂️

Cuando tienes muchas medidas, es súper normal perder tiempo buscando “la correcta” y sentir que el modelo se vuelve un caos. En este video te muestro cómo organizar tus métricas con carpetas desde la vista de modelo:

✅ Agrupa medidas por “% / porcentajes”
✅ Crea una carpeta para “inteligencia de tiempo” (MTD, YTD, etc.)
✅ Mantén tu tabla de métricas limpia y más fácil de usar

📌 Guarda este post para cuando tu modelo empiece a crecer.

#PowerBI #DataAnalytics #BusinessIntelligence #DAX #Dashboard

La pregunta incómoda:
 
¿Tus reportes están diseñados para decidir o solo para informar?
 
La mayoría de los dashboards corporativos no están construidos para tomar decisiones.

Están diseñados para justificar reuniones.
 
Para mostrar actividad.
Para que nadie asuma responsabilidad.
Pero no cambian el negocio.
 
Un KPI sin objetivo estratégico es solo ruido elegante.
Un reporte sin decisión asociada es documentación histórica.

Un dashboard sin impacto medible es decoración corporativa.
 
El problema no es que falten datos.
 
Es que sobra información y falta claridad.
 
Si no respondemos estas preguntas, el coste es real:
 
– ¿Qué decisión concreta activa este indicador?
– ¿Quién es responsable?
– ¿Qué resultado esperamos mover?
– ¿Qué haremos distinto si el número cambia?
 
Si no existe esta cadena mínima:
 
Objetivo → KPI → Dato confiable → Insight → Decisión → Resultado → Aprendizaje
 
No hay gestión basada en datos.
 
Hay reporting.
 
Y el reporting no transforma empresas.
 
La transformación comienza cuando los datos dejan de ser un fin y se convierten en un sistema de decisión trazable.

Hay profesionales que ejecutan reportes.
Y otros que entienden el negocio, anticipan escenarios y usan los datos para influir en las decisiones que importan.
Hoy, el valor no está en saber usar una herramienta.

Está en conectar información con estrategia y datos con dirección.

Eso es Business & Data Analytics aplicado al mundo real.

La analítica ya no es soporte.
Es liderazgo.

Comenta la palabra "Bootcamp" y conoce más.

¿Sigues haciendo reportes manuales y copiando datos en Excel que nadie termina de confiar?

El problema no es que trabajes mal.
El problema es que el modelo ya cambió.

Hoy las empresas competitivas deciden con datos automatizados, trazables y visuales.

Si no sabes construir eso, no estás decidiendo:
estás reaccionando.

Comenta Bootcamp y aprende cómo avanzar 📶

🎯 ¿Te estás preparando para el examen PL-300 de Microsoft?
Este video es para ti 👇

El PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst) no solo evalúa si sabes usar Power BI, sino cómo razonas con el modelo de datos, especialmente en temas de seguridad y administración 🔐📊

En este video analizamos una pregunta real tipo examen y la llevamos a la práctica en Power BI Desktop y Power BI Service para entender:

✔️ Cómo funcionan múltiples roles de seguridad
✔️ La diferencia clave entre aplicar reglas con OR vs AND
✔️ Qué datos ve realmente un usuario cuando pertenece a más de un rol
✔️ Por qué este detalle suele ser una trampa común en el examen

No es solo responder la pregunta.
Es entender la lógica que Microsoft espera que domines 🧠

Si estás estudiando para el PL-300, este tipo de ejercicios marca la diferencia entre memorizar… y aprobar con criterio 🚀

RLS Dinámico con jerarquía + región

🌍 Cuando la seguridad necesita más contexto, el RLS puede escalar.

En este escenario combinamos:
• Rol (gerente o analista)
• Jerarquía organizacional
• Región

El resultado:
• Gerentes ven los datos de su región y sus analistas
• Analistas ven únicamente su información
• Todo desde un solo modelo de datos 📊

Diseñar bien el modelo es lo que permite que Power BI escale de forma segura y profesional 🚀

RLS Dinámico con jerarquía (Gerentes y Analistas)

👥 ¿Qué pasa cuando un mismo reporte debe servir tanto a analistas como a gerentes?

Con RLS dinámico basado en jerarquía organizacional, puedes definir reglas claras:
• Los analistas solo ven sus propios datos
• Los gerentes ven su información y la de todos sus colaboradores

Todo desde un único reporte, utilizando relaciones entre empleados, gerentes y ventas 🧩

Menos reportes 📉
Más control 🔐
Mejor gobierno del dato 📈

Tomar decisiones con datos es hablar el idioma de la dirección:

Priorizar, justificar, ejecutar y medir resultados que importan.

🔴 No más intuición.
🔴 No más reportes sin acción.

¿Hoy tus reportes están influyendo en decisiones reales en tu empresa?

BIFF & The Boe Present: “The Weight of Water” with Director Michael Brown, screening July 28.

Winner of the 2019 Boulder International Film Festival “Call to Action” Award, plus four other national film festival awards, “The Weight of Water” follows the story of blind thrill seeker Erik Weihenmayer. For this epic challenge, Erik solo kayaks the entire Grand Canyon and navigates treacherous waters, including Lava Falls.

When Erik became the first blind person to summit Everest, Boulder-based adventure filmmaker Michael Brown was there with cameras rolling, and the award-winning film “Farther Than the Eye Can See” was the result. When Erik wanted to solo kayak the length of the Grand Canyon, Michael adapted his skills to film the endeavor, capturing the incredible story of a blind man’s quest to conquer his fear of drowning.

“It’s so hard to be fully in the moment because there’s so much fear, there’s so much anxiety, it’s like a person looking through a window at an experience rather than being in the experience.” – Erik Weihenmayer

Award-winning Boulder-based filmmaker Michael Brown (Director) will attend and do a Q&A at the screening. 

Catch “The Weight of Water” on Tuesday, July 28, at The Boe. Tickets available at link in bio!

BIFF and The Boe present: “City Slickers” - a Colorado150 Film Festival selection, screening July 21.

In this Western comedy, Billy Crystal plays Mitch Robbins, the Manhattan yuppie on the verge of a midlife crisis. Joined by his best friends Ed and Phil, the trio set out to reignite their masculinity and conquer their fear of aging. Now, the utterly unprepared thrill-seekers are playing cowhands on a real-life, two-week cattle drive from New Mexico to Colorado to find freedom. Will the clueless city slickers ever become real cowboys?

The only Oscar it won was for Jack Palance for Best Supporting Actor, but the Southwestern landscape nearly steals the show. The gorgeous photography of the high mountain desert captures the essence of Durango, featuring the sprawling ranches and nearly 2 million acres of wild national forest surrounding the city. Scenes from the movie were filmed at a ranch in La Plata County, Colorado, a place immortalized in Westerns such as “Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid” and “A Ticket to Tomahawk”. 

Catch “City Slickers” on Tuesday, July 21, at The Boe. Tickets available at link in bio!

A Colorado150 Film Festival selection.

Before they owned Colorado’s favorite campy restaurant Casa Bonita, Matt Stone and Trey Parker were film students at CU-Boulder. This feature film was created only 30 episodes into their hit series “South Park,” making it one of the fastest TV-to-film adaptations in television history. The film follows Eric Cartman and his friends as they infiltrate an R-rated movie. The town is scandalized, left believing that Canada is to blame for the kids’ new level of vulgarity.

NEW: Oxford has been named the world’s number one university for a record-breaking 11th consecutive year in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings.

Oxford has held the top spot since 2017 - the longest run at number one in the rankings’ history.

Vice-Chancellor Professor Irene Tracey said: ‘This is something to celebrate and it is a testament to the extraordinary talent and dedication of our academics, students and professional services staff across the collegiate University.’

This year’s rankings considered a record 2,297 universities from 118 countries, with Oxford achieving the maximum score of 100 across eight metrics.

#oxforduniversity

childPosts.alt: Aerial view of Oxford’s Radcliffe Camera and surrounding University buildings at sunset. Text reads: ‘Oxford named best university in the world for record 11 years in a row.’

Quote from Professor Irene Tracey, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Oxford: ‘What particularly pleases me is the depth and breadth of excellence this result reflects. From the quality and impact of our research to our thriving innovation ecosystem and global networks, all alongside uncompromising and outstanding teaching and student experience. This is something to celebrate and it is a testament to the extraordinary talent and dedication of our academics, students and professional services staff across the collegiate University as well as the rich higher education environment in which we operate. Rankings are, of course, only one measure of what makes a great university, and our focus remains firmly on what matters: pushing the boundaries of knowledge, educating exceptional students and putting our research and teaching to work for the benefit of society and the planet.’

PCAF Stories Kids is BACK, and this year we’re on the hunt for friendship in the wild and wonderful universe of comics!

🇦🇺 🇧🇪 BRUSSELS COMIC ARTIST RESIDENCY PROGRAM APPLICATIONS CLOSE TONIGHT 🇧🇪 🇦🇺

The Perth Comic Arts Festival, in association with the Musée de la Bande Dessinée @comicartmuseumbxl, is very proud to present the first comics-artist residency in Brussels available to Western Australian artists.
Between October and December 2026, for three weeks, the Museum is hosting Belgian and international comic artists in Brussels for an artistic residency. This residency, with the support of PCAF, is available to a Western Australian comics-maker. The residency will bring together artists to share, explore, and inspire one another.

The Museum undertakes to organize the residency with the Artist to enable them to work optimally on their project, following the Artist for the duration of the residency and doing its best to:
🗯️ Provide help and advice on their work
🗯️ Share professional contacts and facilitate meetings
🗯️ Invite the Artist to public or networking events that would happen during its stay
🗯️ Include the Artist in the Museum activities, if the programming allows it
🗯️ The Museum will also provide the artist with 50€ per diem for up to 21 days

PCAF will support the artist by:
🗯️ Assisting the artist with finding accommodation in Brussels for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $3000 AUD towards accommodation costs for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $2000 AUD towards return flight costs to Brussels from Perth

WHO CAN APPLY?
Comic artists meeting all of the following criteria:
🗯️ A practicing comics artist based in Western Australia with a graphic novel or long-form comic currently in process
🗯️ An Australian citizen or Permanent Resident with an up-to-date passport
🗯️ At least 18 years of age

Please head to pcaf.org.au/2026-brussels-residency for full details on the residency and the application guidelines!

IMPORTANT DATES
🗯️ Applications open: 26th of July, 2026
🗯️ Applications close: 14th of August, 2026
🗯️ Applicants notified: 31st of August, 2026
🗯️ Residency Period: 3 continuous weeks, between the 10th of October and 15th of December (to be decided in consultation with PCAF and the Museum).

Mark your calendars! 🚀 Reservations to experience the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, the permanent home of space shuttle Endeavour, open to the public Wednesday, October 21, at 9:30 a.m.

California Science Center Members get early reservation access beginning Monday, October 19, at 9:30 a.m.

The new Air and Space Center opens Friday, November 13, bringing Endeavour's launch-ready configuration, 100 aerospace artifacts, and 100 new hands-on exhibits to life across three spectacular galleries: the Samuel Oschin Shuttle Gallery, Korean Air Aviation Gallery, and the Kent Kresa Space Gallery.

General admission to the California Science Center is free, but advance reservations are strongly encouraged due to anticipated high demand. A $4 reservation service fee applies per person and is waived for Members.

🎟️ Reserve your visit starting October 21 at our link in bio or californiasciencecenter.org/reservations. Guests may make up to 19 individual reservations per entry time. 

📞 Groups of 20 or more must make a group reservation by calling (213) 744-2019. 

❗This is your last chance to become a Member to take advantage of early reservation access starting October 19 before they open up to all guests and an exclusive Members Day on November 1! Become a Member at our link in bio or californiasciencecenter.org/member.

#CaliforniaScienceCenter #SamuelOschinAirAndSpaceCenter

Our entire California Science Center team is excited to announce that the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center opens November 13, 2026! 🚀

The California Science Center's Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center will showcase Endeavour in the world's only complete, authentic space shuttle system, displayed 20 stories tall in launch position.

In the Samuel Oschin Shuttle Gallery, you will embark on the journey of an astronaut:
🚀 Sit inside a replica flight deck and interact with joysticks, switches, lights, buttons and pedals, like those the shuttle commander and pilot would operate
🚀 Plunge 45 feet in elevation on the Shuttle Descent Slide, experiencing the sights and sounds of a space shuttle landing
🚀 Ascend 140 feet aboard a gantry-style elevator alongside the space shuttle stack like an astronaut preparing for launch

This transformative 200,000 square-foot expansion to the California Science Center will feature 100 rare and historic aerospace objects and 100 hands-on, interactive exhibits. In addition to the Samuel Oschin Shuttle Gallery, you'll investigate scientific and engineering principles of atmospheric flight in the Korean Air Aviation Gallery and launch into the universe of space exploration in the Kent Kresa Space Gallery.

Artifact and exhibit installation continues before the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center is ready for liftoff. Stay tuned for information on when timed reservations open—Science Center Members will receive priority access to reservations before the general public! Become a Member now at our link in bio.

🗓️ 14 years ago today, space shuttle Endeavour completed its 3-day, 3-night, 12-mile journey to its new home at the California Science Center. We are still so grateful to everyone who helped along its journey. 💜

Now, you can help carry Endeavour's mission forward. 🚀

Join Team Endeavour by sponsoring a space shuttle thermal tile and support the completion of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, Endeavour’s permanent home. Sponsor a tile by December 31 and receive a limited one-year Explorer Membership, with Members-only benefits including early access to reserve tickets and waived service fees for advance reservations.

Tile sponsorships begin at $1,000 and may be fulfilled in 10 automatic monthly payments. Your name and dedication will be featured in an interactive display inside the Air and Space Center.

Help us complete our biggest "Endeavour" yet and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers.

🚀 Join Team Endeavour at our link in bio or californiasciencecenter.org/team-endeavour.

On this day in 2011, NASA officially transferred the title and ownership of space shuttle Endeavour to the California Science Center. 🚀 

Former NASA Administrator Charlie Bolden walks down memory lane with us as he shares how the Science Center was selected to receive Endeavour and what it was like to see the space shuttle for the first time since it arrived at the museum in October 2012. 

#CaliforniaScienceCenter #SamuelOschinAirAndSpaceCenter

📆 ONE YEAR AGO 📆

Can you believe that it's been 1 year since the topping out of Endeavour's home, the future Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center? 

🚀Relive the ceremonial topping out of the Air and Space Center's diagrid structure! 

#CaliforniaScienceCenter #SamuelOschinAirAndSpaceCenter

📆 3 Years Ago 📆 Our Solid Rocket Motors' traveled home to the California Science Center! 🚀

The SRMs were the final space shuttle element to arrive at the Science Center in the lead up to the historic Go For Stack process to stack Endeavour in launch configuration. 

The SRMs comprise the largest part of the Solid Rocket Boosters (SRBs). During the space shuttle program, twin 15-story reusable SRBs would work with the space shuttle main engine to ignite and produce more than 6-million pounds of thrust—the majority of what was needed to lift a shuttle off the launch pad. 

The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center opens November 13! Are you ready for launch? 🚀

We are excited to announce our first performance since 2024 (and only show in 2026) as part of @__ab100__, a landmark weekend of music and celebration set in the Pays Basque on October 17th & 18th.

AB100 is less a traditional festival than a gathering of artists, friends, and collaborators. At its heart, AB100 is a celebration of friendship in music, shining a light on the deep connections fostered by @aarondessner and @brycedessner and the community of artists they have brought together on the occasion of their 50th birthdays. 

The two-day programme unfolds across Biarritz and San Sebastián before culminating in a special one-off performance by The National & Friends at the Kursaal Donostia in the Spanish city. 

Performers and collaborators that weekend will include Kevin Morby, Ben Howard, Jon Hopkins, Mina Tindle, Ragnar Kjartansson, Richard Reed Perry, Anaïs Mitchell, Ye Vagabonds, Lisa Hannigan, Angie McMahon, Kate Stables, Pomme and many more to be announced.

Tickets go on sale to the general public *August 10* at 11:30am CET / 5:30am EDT / 2:30am PDT.

For information on the complete programme lineup, as well as future updates, follow @__ab100__

latestPosts.caption:
Curfews in some French cities could be extended on Tuesday, the country’s Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said, after restrictions helped keep the peace on Monday night following a weekend in which protests deteriorated into looting and rioting.⁠
⁠
Curfews were implemented on Monday night in parts of Paris, with similar measures in Lyon. Protests were banned in Marseille, while Nice, Lille, Denain and Douai set curfews for minors in some neighbourhoods.⁠
⁠
The government is under pressure to reassert control after inadequate planning led to law enforcement being overwhelmed at the weekend as protests about the high cost of living and education funding splintered into marauding groups of rioters. Thousands of businesses were damaged, ranging from international chains to small independent shops. ⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more. ⁠
⁠
Picture credit: Guillaume Saligot / AFP via Getty Images⁠

Alberta looks set to remain part of Canada rather than back a separation process that would plunge the country into a crisis at a time when President Donald Trump has threatened to make it the 51st US state.⁠
⁠
Voters in the province were asked on Monday if they would support a referendum on whether to leave Canada. Based on preliminary results from CBC, Canada’s national broadcaster, 77% voted against holding a poll while 23% voted in favour. With about a third per cent of results counted, the broadcaster projected that the remain vote would prevail.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more. ⁠
⁠
Picture credit: Megan Albu / AFP via Getty Images⁠

From booking train tickets to making doctor’s appointments, everyday life is becoming increasingly digital, with many older people struggling to keep pace.⁠
⁠
Claer Barrett explains why banks and businesses must do more to support older customers.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more.

Masked figures wielded a road barrier as a battering ram against the windows of the Louis Vuitton boutique on Paris’s upscale Place Vendôme on Saturday, cheered on by dozens of black-clad figures. The looters never made it inside, but it was close.⁠
⁠
Other retailers were less fortunate, with some stores ransacked and defaced. Now authorities are working to stop stolen goods being resold online through platforms such as Vinted, Amazon and eBay, after a weekend of rioting and looting across France.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more.⁠
⁠
Photo credit: Jeff Pachoud/AFP/Getty Images⁠
⁠
Image description: A police officer takes photographs of the broken frontage window of a Louis Vuitton store in Lyon. Text on image reads: Louis Vuitton and Hermès among luxury retailers looted in French riots

Could the midterm elections mark a turning point for American democracy or has the country already gone too far down the road towards authoritarianism?⁠
⁠
In the first of a six-part series of interviews with leading historians and political analysts, Martin Wolf speaks to the scholar and former Republican adviser Robert Kagan, who has spent a decade warning about Trump's authoritarian ambitions. ⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to listen to the full podcast.

Employers are trying all sorts of things to combat fraudulent AI use in the recruitment process. ⁠
⁠
There are jobseekers who use chatbots to bluff their way into jobs they’re not capable of, or pay 'interview mules' to complete assessments for them. More dangerously, there are hackers who try to get hired with false identities in order to access internal systems, and even remote IT workers who turn out to be based in North Korea. ⁠
⁠
The research company Gartner has predicted that one in four candidate profiles worldwide will be fake by 2028.⁠
⁠
All this is leading to a culture clash inside companies, writes @sarahoconnorft.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio for the full story.

David Miliband, the UK’s former foreign secretary and head of the International Rescue Committee since 2013, sat down with the FT's Patrick Jenkins to discuss his new hope in UK politics and hinted at a possible return.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more.

President Emmanuel Macron has refused the French interior minister’s offer to resign over the botched police response to protests that stunned the country and led to thousands of arrests over the weekend.⁠
⁠
Nationwide demonstrations on Saturday that brought together students protesting education conditions and citizens angry about the high cost of living descended into riots and widespread looting, touching off a political firestorm.⁠
⁠
'I have a sense of responsibility to the public, and given the damage that was done, it was only right that I offer my resignation,' Laurent Nuñez said on Monday. ⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more. ⁠
⁠
Picture credit: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images⁠

Anthropic has said it will commit 5 per cent of its shares to a new 'public benefit fund' as it seeks to address public backlash against AI ahead of its planned blockbuster initial public offering.⁠
⁠
The $965bn start-up on Sunday said it would commit the shares, worth around $48bn at its latest valuation, subject to shareholder approval. It plans to add a further 2% of the stock for every 50% increase in the company’s value above an undisclosed baseline.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more. ⁠
⁠
Picture credit: Kent Nishimura/ AFP/ Getty Images⁠

For days this month New Delhi was effectively under lockdown to prevent protests, with scores of security personnel deployed to fend off the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party.⁠
⁠
The FT’s Andres Schipani reports from the Indian capital on the growing unrest.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read more.

Japan is preparing to launch the first return trip to Mars’ orbit, aiming to retrieve physical samples from the moon Phobos and search for further possible signs of life.⁠
⁠
An H3 rocket is set to blast off from Tanegashima Space Center on Tuesday carrying a spacecraft that will make a five-year voyage. ‘We’ve been to Mars a lot of times, but we’ve never come back, so it’s a huge milestone for space exploration,’ said Sanjeev Gupta, a planetary scientist at Imperial College London.⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio to read the full story.⁠
⁠
Photo credit: Science Photo Library/Reuters Connect⁠
⁠
Image description: An illustration showing a terraformed Mars with blue oceans of liquid water and clouds, and Phobos orbiting above the surface. Text on image reads: Japan leads mission to make first return trip to Mars

The French government faces a fresh crisis after police on Saturday struggled to contain attacks on businesses and public buildings, including city halls and police stations, in cities from Marseille to Paris, Bordeaux and Lyon. Thousands of black-clad and masked rioters hijacked broader peaceful protests by students and people marching nationwide against the high cost of living. An estimated 550,000 demonstrators are estimated to have turned out overall.⁠
⁠
A record number of people were arrested in Paris and some 500 police officers and firefighters were injured.⁠
⁠
The rioting comes six months ahead of a highly uncertain election to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, piling pressure on the government, which has been grappling with student protests over conditions in high schools while trying to pass a budget for next year in the face of bond market jitters about France’s ability to rein in its deficit. ⁠
⁠
Tap the link in our bio for the latest updates.⁠
⁠

When you think of Sicilian lemons, bright yellow probably comes to mind—but there’s another citrus that’s just as fascinating. 🍋❤️

Grown in limited quantities around Syracuse, the red lemon (Citrus limonimedica pigmentata) is one of Sicily’s rarest fruits. Known for its reddish-orange peel, delicate aroma, and milder flavor, it’s a local specialty that’s treasured for everything from desserts and preserves to traditional recipes.

It’s a reminder that even in a destination as well-known as Sicily, there are still unique discoveries waiting to be found.

Had you ever heard of a red lemon before? 👇

📍 Sicily, Italy 🇮🇹

For anyone who’s trying their best right now, remember that growth doesn’t always happen during the easy seasons of life. Sometimes the moments that challenge you the most are the ones that teach you just how strong and capable you really are.

You don’t have to have everything figured out to be proud of how far you’ve come. Learning to accept your imperfections, recognize your weaknesses, and grow from your mistakes is part of becoming the person you’re meant to be.

There may have been months when everything felt heavy, when your mind was filled with worries and you couldn’t see a way forward. But just like flowers bloom after the rain, beautiful things can still grow from seasons you thought would never end.

Every setback doesn’t have to mean you’ve failed, and every delay doesn’t mean your dreams are out of reach. Trust that God has already placed something valuable inside you, even on the days when you struggle to believe in yourself.

Keep showing up, keep learning, and give yourself permission to grow at your own pace.

Leave a ❤️ if you believe your hardest seasons can lead to some of your most beautiful beginnings.

A gentle reminder for your heart today, the way you treat people says a lot about the kind of person you choose to be. A little kindness, patience, and respect can make someone’s day better in ways you may never realize.

Everyone you meet is carrying something you might not know about, whether it’s stress, sadness, or a difficult situation they’re trying to work through. Sometimes the way you speak to someone can either add to what they’re carrying or remind them that there are still good people in this world.

You don’t have to agree with everyone to treat them with dignity, and you don’t have to understand someone’s entire story to show them compassion. Listening without judging, speaking with kindness, and being mindful of your words are simple ways to make others feel valued.

Respect should never depend on someone’s job, appearance, background, or what they can do for you. Every person deserves to be treated with basic human decency, especially during moments when life is already difficult enough.

Choose to be someone who makes others feel comfortable, heard, and appreciated wherever you go.

Leave a ❤️ if you believe kindness and respect should always be part of how we treat one another.

For the person who’s been carrying so much in silence, this is your reminder to be proud of yourself. You’ve made it through moments that nobody knows about, fought battles you never spoke of, and somehow found the strength to keep going.

Not everyone will understand what it took for you to get where you are today, and that’s okay. Some of your biggest victories happened quietly, on days when simply getting out of bed and facing the world took everything you had.

You don’t need anyone to recognize your struggles for them to matter, and you don’t have to explain your pain to prove how strong you’ve been. The tears you wiped away, the worries you carried alone, and the times you chose to keep trying are all part of your story.

Give yourself credit for the progress you’ve made, even if you’re still figuring things out along the way. Healing isn’t always something others can see, and sometimes the most meaningful growth happens when nobody is watching.

Be gentle with yourself and remember how far you’ve already come, because you deserve to feel proud of the person you’re becoming.

Leave a ❤️ if you’ve survived battles nobody knows about and you’re still finding the courage to move forward.

Slowing down, appreciating the little things, and being grateful for the gift of another day.
If your mind immediately notices the pressure, the problems, and what’s missing, you’re not alone. But you can practice noticing something different. ❤️

You can train your mind to notice the good without ignoring what’s hard.

Comment “GRATITUDE” and I’ll send you the details for my 3 Minute Gratitude Journal + your instant bonuses so we can start together.

For anyone who’s been feeling discouraged lately, remember that just because something hasn’t happened yet doesn’t mean it never will. Sometimes the waiting feels endless, especially when you’ve been doing your best and wondering when things will finally start falling into place.

You’ve already survived so many difficult moments that once felt impossible to get through. Don’t let one hard chapter make you forget all the strength, patience, and courage that brought you this far.

Not everything is within your control, including how other people treat you or how quickly life changes. What you can choose is how you respond, where you put your energy, and what you allow to take away your peace.

Give yourself permission to grow at your own pace without comparing your journey to anyone else’s. The things that truly matter to you may take time, and even the smallest steps forward are worth celebrating.

Keep showing up for yourself, trust that your efforts matter, and remember that your story is still unfolding.

Leave a ❤️ if you’re choosing to keep going, protect your peace, and believe that better days are still ahead.

A reminder for the part of you that’s still healing, you’ve come too far to forget how much strength it took to get where you are today. There were days when you felt completely lost, yet somehow you found the courage to keep moving forward.

Sometimes we forget how difficult certain chapters of our lives were once we’ve finally made it through them. The sleepless nights, the tears nobody saw, and the battles you fought quietly are all reminders of what you’ve overcome.

Please don’t feel guilty for protecting the peace you worked so hard to find. You don’t have to return to situations, relationships, or habits that once made you question your worth just because they feel familiar.

Healing doesn’t mean you’ll never have difficult days again, and it certainly doesn’t mean you have to be strong every moment. It means learning to recognize what hurts you, choosing healthier paths, and giving yourself permission to grow beyond the person you used to be.

You’ve worked so hard to find your way back to yourself, and that progress deserves to be protected.

Leave a ❤️ if you’re choosing peace, healing, and a better chapter for yourself.

Maybe your heart needed this reminder today, especially if you’ve been worrying about things you can’t control. Whatever you’re facing right now, please don’t lose hope that life can still get better.

Sometimes we spend so much time thinking about what could go wrong that we forget how quickly things can change for the better. The answers you’re waiting for might not come today, but that doesn’t mean there’s nothing good ahead of you.

You don’t need to have everything figured out right now, and you certainly don’t need to carry every worry all at once. Give yourself permission to take things one day at a time and trust that you’re doing the best you can with what you have.

There will be moments when life feels uncertain, but those moments don’t mean your story is headed in the wrong direction. You’ve already made it through so many difficult days, and there’s still so much love, happiness, and peace left for you to experience.

Whatever is weighing on your heart tonight, I hope you find a little comfort knowing that this difficult season doesn’t have to last forever.

Leave a ❤️ if you’re choosing to believe that everything will be alright.
Type YES to claim it

In case you needed this today, remember that even the smallest acts of kindness can make someone’s day a little brighter. A simple smile, a thoughtful compliment, or a genuine thank you might mean more to someone than you’ll ever realize.

Sometimes we get so caught up in our busy lives that we forget how much the little things matter. Taking a moment to show someone you care can leave a beautiful memory that stays with them long after that moment has passed.

For anyone who hasn’t felt like themselves lately, please remember that your light hasn’t disappeared just because life has been difficult. Give yourself the same patience and kindness you would offer someone you love, because you deserve that gentleness too.

You don’t have to have everything figured out or prove yourself to everyone around you. Sometimes growth means choosing peace over arguments, trusting yourself through uncertain seasons, and finding the courage to take one small step toward something better.

Keep being kind, protect your peace, and remember that your presence can make a difference in ways you may never see.

Leave a ❤️ if you believe the little things in life often mean the most.

latestPosts.caption: You don’t need to drive far from Melbourne to find views this insane! We were blown away by the scenery and pristine ocean blues 💙 It’s the perfect adventure for your next weekend getaway. Please check tide times, signs and local conditions if swimming at Sorrento Back Beach or any other beach in Victoria to avoid dangerous conditions @visitmelbourne AD

Visitors to the iconic Twelve Apostles will now be able to experience the new Keerray Woorroong Visitor Centre 🎉⁣
⁣
Located on @visitgreatoceanroad, the new venue features interactive displays, local dining and retail spaces, a rooftop observation deck as well as a welcome garden celebrating local Easter Maar culture ✨⁣
⁣
📍 The Keerray Woorroong Visitor Centre is located just under three hours from Melbourne, on the lands of the Eastern Maar people⁣
🎟️ Admission is currently free, however you do need to book in advance - you can do so via the @twelveapostlesprecinct website⁣
📸 @twelveapostlesprecinct⁣
⁣
#12Apostles #TwelveApostles #Victoria

Bendigo is home to some of the most beautiful heritage buildings in the state. And what better time to explore than spring! 😍🌸⁣
⁣
📍 Bendigo Town Hall, @explorebendigo, a two-hour drive from Melbourne, on lands of the Dja Dja Wurrung people⁣
📸 @cindyvains⁣
⁣
#Victoria #Bendigo⁣
⁣

Il vostro “gusto estetico” non è al di sopra delle leggi.

Ieri abbiamo portato Stop Tassa Etica al Festival Internazionale di Pavia, insieme a Valentina Nappi e Fabio Salamida, partendo dalla domanda «Chi decide cosa è morale?»

Uno Stato laico non può usare il fisco per imporre una pedagogia dei costumi, né per giudicare la moralità dei cittadini. Quando lo fa, partorisce norme discriminatorie, in contrasto con i principi costituzionali ed economicamente dannose per il nostro Paese.

È sempre bello confrontarsi sulle battaglie per la laicità dello Stato, la libertà individuale e per pretendere leggi fondate sulla razionalità, non sul moralismo.
